item.title: Talocrural Traction
patientPosition: Supine or long sitting with ankle near resting position.
contact: Cup calcaneus/talus region with broad hands.
forceDirection: Distraction in line with talocrural treatment plane/foot axis as taught.
mistakes: Using strong traction in acute sprain.
safety: Avoid fracture or unstable acute injury.
item.visualCue: Leg fixed → Talocrural joint distracted → Re-test dorsiflexion.

subTechniques.name: Talocrural Traction
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Reduce compression sensitivity and prepare for translatoric glides.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine or long sitting with the ankle near its resting position.
subTechniques.contact: Stabilize the distal tibia/fibula and grasp the talus/calcaneus close to the joint.
subTechniques.direction: Apply sustained distraction perpendicular to the talocrural treatment plane.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Keep the traction at the talocrural joint rather than simply pulling the forefoot.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid fracture or acute syndesmotic instability.

subTechniques.name: Posterior Talar Translatoric Glide
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve dorsiflexion when posterior translatoric motion is limited.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine/long sitting or weight-bearing as appropriate with the tibia stabilized.
subTechniques.contact: Broad contact over the anterior talus, avoiding neurovascular compression.
subTechniques.direction: Apply a sustained posterior glide parallel to the treatment plane.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Use the weight-bearing lunge as the main quick re-test.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid acute ankle instability or fracture.
